Use all FH* codes for: conspiracy thrillers, disaster thrillers, Eco-thrillers, classic thrillers, assassination thrillers, vigilante justice thrillers, kidnapping or murder thrillers, domestic thrillers. Use all FH* codes with: other F* codes as appropriate for different types of thriller or suspense fiction that do not have a unique code, such as FL* for Sci-fi thrillers, FRM for Romantic thrillers, FK for Horror thrillers, FJM* for military thrillers, FV for historical thrillers, JBGX for thrillers about conspiracies, FXS for Social thrillers, FF* for crime thrillers

Also class here: Spy novels, stories featuring cold war spies, secret agents, undercover agents, spy agencies or intelligence agencies, counter-intelligence, state intelligence services, intelligence officers, secret services, secret police, spying or intelligence gathering, assassins or assassination plots in the world of espionage, etc

Also class here: thrillers featuring white-collar crimes, crimes of corruption, fraud or greed. Use for: thrillers in which the financial system, the world of finance and money, the financial markets, the economy, big business, world of corporations, multinational or transnational business or corporations, financial professionals, business people, corporate bosses, wealthy business families or dynasties, or similar play a major role
Anlatının önemli parçaları olarak bilimsel, teknolojik (bilgisayar dahil), tıbbi vb unsurları içeren gerilim eserleri için kullanın

Use for: thrillers that usually feature something used for medical purposes becoming a weapon or threat, such as a virus, often featuring medical practitioners as key characters, biological threats, pandemics, medical forensic practitioners, etc

Also class here: Courtroom drama thrillers, thrillers featuring lawyers, judges, prosecutors or other legal settings or roles, or politicians, the world of politics or political settings, including political plots, political assassinations, political conspiracies, political targeted killings, etc
Kutsal kadeh vb. gibi, antik, gizli ya da ezoterik bilgilere dayanan gerilim hikayeleri için kullanın

Use for: thrillers based around criminal organizations, the criminal underworld, the mob, the mafia, crime syndicates, criminal gangs, contract killers, hired killers, professional gunmen, assassins, hitmen or hitwomen, criminal gangs, criminal feuds, criminal families, gangland crimes, gangsters, gritty urban crime, etc Ayrıca bakınız: FFL

Use for: thrillers based around mass murderers, serial killers, spree killings, thrill killers, angel of mercy or angel of death type killers, etc. Use with: FK* for horror stories that include serial killers
Use for: thrillers based around potential terrorist actions, acts of terrorism, terrorist plots, political terrorism, conspiracies to commit acts of terror, anti-terror plots, etc

Also class here: Domestic thrillers. Use for: thrillers that deal with a psychological narrative, or are told from the viewpoint of psychologically stressed characters, or where the plot concentrates on investigations of the psychologies of the principal characters, thrillers that examine things like perception, reality, the mind, identity, existence or purpose, etc Ayrıca bakınız: FXM

Use all FJ* codes for: adventure stories, stories of exploration, classic adventure or action stories. Use for: works that primarily emphasise physical, and sometimes violent, action, that often have a sense of danger and are meant to give the reader a sense of excitement or adventure Ayrıca bakınız: FH
Also class here: wuxia, Bukyō. Use with: FM*, FV*, XQ* codes plus TIME PERIOD 3* Qualifiers as appropriate
Geçmiş zamanda geçen tüm macera romanları için kullanın; daha özel FGM* kodlarını eğer uygunsa tercih edin. COĞRAFİ ve/ya DÖNEM kalifiyerlerini uygun olduğunca kullanmaya çalışın Ayrıca bakınız: FJM

Also class here: Special forces stories, historical military fiction. Use for: stories that primarily emphasise the action or adventure side of war or combat. Use with: PLACE 1* and/or TIME PERIOD 3* Qualifiers to indicate setting for historical war or combat fiction. Prefer: other F* codes and TIME PERIOD 3* qualifiers for works where war or conflict is part of the background of the story or that examine the impact of war but where the primary theme could not be seen as action or adventure

Also class here: stories set during the French Revolutionary Wars, the Coalition Wars, the Peninsular Wars, the War of 1812 or any other associated war or military campaign of this period. Use with: PLACE 1* and/or TIME PERIOD 3* Qualifiers to indicate setting as appropriate
Also class here: naval and maritime fiction, nautical fiction. Use for: adventure or action stories featuring seafarers, pirates, sailors, fishermen and so on, or largely set at sea

Use all FK* codes for: monster literature, Lovecraftian horror, cosmic horror, Eldritch horror, psychological horror, folk horror, body horror, transformative gore, survival horror, haunted house horror, extreme horror, demonic horror or any stories that provoke or inspire feelings of dread, fear and terror, or are intended to disturb, frighten or scare, using psychological or supernatural elements, or any story that includes a ghost, or the possibility of ghosts, or a characters belief in ghosts. Use all FK* codes with: VXQ* codes if appropriate, for example with VXQG for ghost stories, VXQM2 for vampire, werewolf or shifter horror, VXQM3 for zombie horror, VXQM5 for demon horror, VXWT for stories featuring evil witches and other F* codes, for example, FU* Comedy horror, FL* for Horror Science fiction, FP for Erotic horror, FV for Historical Horror, FLQ or FDB for Post-Apocalyptic Horror, FF* or FH* for Crime horror or thrillers with a horror plot, FHX or FXM for Quiet or psychological horror, FYL for Gothic horror, or with 5* Qualifiers, for example, 5HPD for Christmas Horror, 5HRD for Winter Horror, etc Ayrıca bakınız: FMT FHX
Sınıflandırın: 1950’den önce yayımlanmış korku ve hayalet hikayeleri
Use for: supernatural fiction, horror or ghost stories set in the present day or contemporary settings, typically first published in the last few decades

Use for: works where major themes of the story deal with the darker side of witchcraft, spiritualism, psychic phenomena, demonic possession, satanism, mysterious or secret knowledge, or other paranormal phenomenon

Use all FL* codes with: other subjects codes or qualifiers for different types of SF that do not have a unique code, for example, FU for Comical (humorous) science fiction, Sci-fi comedy, 5PS for LGBTQIA+ science fiction, 6JM for Indigenous Futurisms in SF, with 6AR for Afrofuturism (African-American / Black American / African diaspora SF), or with 6AS Africanfuturism (African) in SF, FK* for Science fiction with horror stories Ayrıca bakınız: FD FDM
Sınıflandırın: 1970’ten önce basılan bilim kurgu için

Also class here: Chuanyue, Isekai, stories based on travelling to a past or future time via time loops, time machines, time slips, time portals, accidental time travel, alternate timestreams, time warp, temporal paradoxes, experiencing time in reverse, communication from the future, being stuck in a time-loop, stories where time is a significant element, different spacetime geometries, wormholes in spacetime, stories based on the quantum mechanics of time travel, temporal war, etc. Use with: FM* codes for time travel or time slip fantasy stories, with FDK for alternate history science fiction, featuring alternate futures, different timestreams, multiple time paths

Use for: science fiction that emphasises scientific detail and / or accuracy, or that use science that exist within the realm of scientific possibility or do not go outside the known physical laws of the universe

Use for: science fiction stories that have a more positive, lighter and more comforting, feel-good or uplifting approach to telling the story, and that tend not to create any anxiety, often featuring narratives around hope and optimism, friends or friendship, found or chosen family, communities, and where conflicts or crisis are usually resolved through communication and understanding, with the help of community and friends, often stories with elements of science fiction, but where world-building is not a major element
Sınıflandırın: 19. yy buhar gücünün tekrar dominant güç olarak ortaya çıktığı alternatif gelecekler üzerine yazılmış bilim kurgular için
Sınıflandırın: siberpunk, yüksek teknolojiye sahip bir toplumda marjinalize edilmiş ya da değersiz bir hayat sürdüren karakter üzerine kurulmuş bilim kurgular için

Also class here: Nanopunk, Cyber-noir, solarpunk, techno-noir. Use for: science fiction based on marginalised or low-life characters in a highly technologically advanced society or focused on the implications of biotechnology or genetic engineering

Also class here: end of the world stories, dying earth, collapsing or collapsed civilization. Use for: stories set in worlds trying to prevent, or experiencing or that have already been affected by an apocalypse event, such as runaway climate change, an impact event, resource depletion, nuclear holocaust, pandemics, plagues, viruses, the end times, a zombie apocalypse, cybernetic revolts, technological singularity, invasion from space, dysgenics, an electromagnetic pulse (EMP), stories of groups of survivors or survival after a catastrophe or cataclysm etc. Use with: FXE for climate fiction or ecological collapse, FXV for stories of journeys through a devastated world or other codes and qualifiers as appropriate
Askeri ortamda geçen veya organize silah kullanımının merkezde yer aldığı bilim kurgu için kullanın Ayrıca bakınız: FLS
Yüksek kültür ve teknolojiye sahip, uzayda geçen bilim kurgu için kullanın
Also class here: first contact, alien invasion, human interaction with extra-terrestrial life forms, alien conspiracies
Also class here: colonisation of space, settlement of planets or moons, exploration of deep space, moon bases, generation ships, terraforming, first landings on other planets, astronauts

Use all FM* codes for: Classic fantasy, other worlds fantasy, Crossworlds fantasy, Futuristic fantasy, Portal fantasy, Parallel worlds, Quest fantasy, Literary fantasy, Hard fantasy. Use all FM* codes with: other codes for different types of fantasy that do not have a unique code, for example, with 5LKE for New Adult Fantasy, 5PX-XA-A for Arthurian fantasy, VXQM1 for dragon fantasy, 5PGM for Christian fantasy, 5PS, 5PT, 5PU or 5PV for LGBTQIA+ fantasy, FXB for coming of age fantasy, FU* for Comic fantasy, 5YH for Anthropomorphic fantasy, FDB or FLQ for dying earth or post-apocalyptic fantasy, FP for erotic fantasy or FRX for Erotic Fantasy Romance, FXP for Political fantasy, FLM for Steampunk fantasy, FJW for Weird west fantasy, FL* for Sword and planet fantasy, 6AU for Academy fantasy, etc
Use for: stories set in alternative or secondary worlds, usually with detailed world building and a complex fictional universe or shared world, and often involving large events or long quests

Also class here: Swashbuckling fantasy. Use for: works of fantasy that concentrate more on the adventures and battles of the hero or main protagonist, rather than the world building, or fantasy stories that feature a hero, anti-hero or morally grey hero going on some sort of quest or any sort of hero‘s journey in a fantasy or supernatural setting where the narrative concentrates more on the adventure rather than building the fantasy world. Use with: other FM* codes as appropriate

Also class here: Medieval, Dark Age, Classical (Greek and Roman), Arabian, Celtic, Fantasy of Manners, Mannerpunk, Flintlock, Gunpowder, Prehistoric, Gaslamp fantasy genres. Use for: fantasy that incorporates fantastic elements, such as magic or elements from myths, into recognisable historic settings, periods, cultures etc. Use with: PLACE 1* and/or TIME PERIOD 3* Qualifiers to indicate setting as appropriate

Use for: fantasy stories that have a more positive, lighter and more comforting, feel-good or uplifting approach to telling the story, and that tend not to create any anxiety, often featuring narratives around hope and optimism, friends or friendship, found or chosen family, communities, and where conflicts or crisis are usually resolved through communication and understanding, with the help of community and friends

Also class here: Magic realism. Use for: works that incorporates fantastic, magical, mythical or supernatural elements into an otherwise real-world or mundane setting, stories that have a largely realistic view of the world but with a few supernatural or magical elements, that are often used to make a point about reality. Use with: FBA or FBC for literary works that incorporate magical realism, for example, those of the kind frequently associated with literature from Latin America or other literary traditions
Sınıflandırın: vampir romansları, vb. Ayrıca bakınız: FRV FRT
Use for: fiction featuring or where the main characters are depicted as superheroes / superheroines or superhumans

Also class here: Grimdark. Use for: fantasy stories with darker and frightening themes, often incorporating elements of horror or that have a gloomy and threatening atmosphere or a sense of horror and dread

Also class here: intrusion fantasy, mundane fantasy. Use for: fantasy set in the present day or contemporary or modern settings or set in a recognisable version of our world, but with elements of fantasy or the supernatural added in

Also class here: Elfpunk, Arcanepunk fantasy, gritty urban fantasy. Use for: fantasy works set in urban settings, often featuring plots where the real modern urban setting and the supernatural or paranormal collide or overlap, or where mythical or supernatural beings and creatures exist in recognisable urban settings. Use with: VXQ* codes as appropriate

Code.CodeDescription: Kurgu gibi anlatılan mit ve efsane
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: Fables. Use all FN* codes for: stories that often have a long and continuous existence through multiple generations, stories that get told and retold, traditional local folktales, tall tales, folklore, folk literature, wisdom tales, cautionary stories, teaching stories, origin tales, or any form of traditional story told or retold. Use for: modern retellings in novel form or collections of traditional tales and stories aimed primarily at adults, or works inspired by these stories Ayrıca bakınız: DBS* QRS* JBGB YFJ YNRU

Code.CodeDescription: Fairy and Folk tales / Fairy tale retellings
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: folk and fairy tales from any culture told in a story form, or fantasy retellings of these stories, fairy tales as fiction, fairy tale fantasy. Use for: modern retellings in novel form or collections of these types of traditional stories aimed primarily at adults, or stories recognisably inspired by traditional fairy stories or that in some way draw from the characters, tropes, themes and symbolism of folklore and fairy tales and where, for example, an author might tell a new story based on a popular fairy tale or character from a classic work, or take a ‘what if’ approach or create a mashup of different genres, for example, fairy tale meets dystopian future Ayrıca bakınız: JBGB YFJ YNXB4

Also class here: Mythological Fiction, Legend fantasy, Mythic fantasy, myths and legends from any culture told in story form, myth or legend retold as fiction, or genres such as mythpunk, godpunk, Shenmo, Gods and Demons fiction, Xianxia, Immortal heroes fiction, Arthurian fiction, Classical (Greek and Roman myths told as stories or retold). Use for: modern retellings in novel form or collections of these types of traditional stories aimed primarily at adults, or stories recognisably inspired by traditional myths or stories that draw from the characters, gods and goddesses, heroes and heroines, tropes, themes and symbolism of myths or legends and where, for example, an author might tell a new story based on a myth, or take a ‘what if’ approach or create a mashup of different genres, for example, mythology crossed with contemporary adventure story. Use with: QRS* or QRR* codes or PLACE1* qualifiers to indicate which tradition, as appropriate Ayrıca bakınız: DBS* JBGB QRS* YFJ YNRU
Use for: stories that feature a trickster character such as a spirit, a deity, a human or an animal, or stories inspired by or retellings of stories about trickster characters from different cultures
Kalifiyer 5X ile beraber kullanın Ayrıca bakınız: FRX
Burada sınıflandırın: “Genç kız romanları”, “kadın romanları” Ayrıca bakınız: FRB FRD

Use all FR* codes for: Love stories, classic romance, slow burn romances. Use all FR* codes with: qualifiers for particular types of romance, for example, with 5H* qualifiers for Holiday Romance, such as 5HRB for summer vacation romance or 5HPD for Christmas romance, 5PS* or other 5P* qualifiers for LGBTQIA+ romances, 5LKS for romance in later life, FL* codes for Science fiction romance, FJ* for action and adventure romance, JBSE for small town romance, 5PB-US-C for Black and African American romance, 5HKU for Romance about marriage, FYL for Gothic romance, 5LKE for New Adult romance, etc
Also class here: Rom-coms. Use for: genre romance and love stories that are also comic, humorous, light hearted or funny in their approach

Use for: romance stories where the main characters live and work in a world most readers can understand, with modern conveniences and current social mores. Use with: other FR* codes and qualifiers for particular sub-genres of contemporary romance, and with qualifiers as appropriate

Use for: romance and love stories that have a more positive, lighter and more comforting, feel-good or uplifting approach to telling the story, and that tend not to create any anxiety, often featuring narratives around hope and optimism, friends or friendship, found or chosen family, communities, and where conflicts or crisis are usually resolved through communication and understanding, with the help of community and friends

Also class here: First job romances, office romances, forbidden workplace romance, love in the workplace, professional romance, renovation romance, working from home romance, boss romance. Use for: Romance stories featuring or set in a working environment, or about a relationship with a work colleague or a romance with a person who is doing some work or working for the other person, for example, someone who is helping to renovate a building, doing some long-term construction work, the gardener, the boss, the CEO, the bodyguard, etc

Also class here: sweetheart romance. Use for: romance that does not contain any strong language or physical intimacy. Use with: FW for religious romance, faith-driven romance, or inspirational romance, and with 5PG* INTEREST Qualifiers as appropriate to indicate a wholesome romance with themes inspired by a particular spiritual belief or faith or with other FR* codes for wholesome romances that are also considered part of another genre romance, with 5PB-US-B for Amish romance, 5PGM for Christian romance, 5PGP for Muslim romance, etc

Also class here: Student romance. Use for: genres of romance fiction often set in an academic environment such as a university or a college campus or an academy, usually featuring university aged characters discovering life as newly adult people, getting their first taste of adult love, romance and often sexual experience. Use with: 5LKE if the main characters and the storyline concern the newly adult or those young adults who have left home for the first time
Not: 1900’lerden önce geçen romantik kurgu, örn. Rejans dönemi için; COĞRAFİ ve DÖNEM kalifiyerlerini de romanın arkaplanını belirtmek için kullanın

Also class here: cowboy, cowgirl, frontier, rancher, rodeo, gaucho, vaquero romances. Use for: romance that takes place in very rural environments, often set on farms, ranches, haciendas, or in small rural communities, usually far from any city and often set in the Western parts of the USA, Mexico or Canada, the pampas of South America, the Australian outback or similar environments. Use with: PLACE 1* Qualifiers to describe setting and TIME PERIOD 3* for historical settings

Also class here: Romance stories featuring extramarital love affairs, cheating love triangles, love triangle jealousy, or other stories featuring some sort of love triangle. Use for: romance stories usually featuring a triangle of relationships and typically involving two people who are competing for the third person’s romantic attention or one person in love with two different people

Also class here: second chance romance, neighbours to lovers, roommates to lovers, opposite attracts, unlikely loves, forbidden love, unforeseen romance, Grump and sunshine romances, sworn off love, etc. Use for: Romance where the plot revolves around a significant change or an adaptation of the nature of an existing relationship between the main characters
Use for: romance stories where the main characters initially have a relationship based on friendship that gradually changes into a strong attraction
Also class here: Rivals to lovers’ romance, Frenemies. Use for: romance stories where the main characters initially have a conflicting relationship that gradually changes into a strong attraction

Also class here: fake-dating, false relationships, fake boyfriend or girlfriend, marriage of convenience romances. Use for: romance stories where the main characters initially have some sort of fake or pretend romantic relationship

Also class here: Stuck together romances, Only-one-bed romances, road trip romances, trapped together romances. Use for: romance stories where the main characters initially are thrown together into close proximity for various reason
Use for: a romance story that also involves a mystery, crime, suspense or thriller storyline but remains primarily a romance story. Use with: other F* genre fiction codes as appropriate

Also class here: Athlete Romance, Football romance, hockey romance, baseball romance, cricket romance, soccer romance, etc. Use for: Romance featuring participants in sports, sports stars, athletes, coaches, owners, agents, sports teams, sporting events, sporting activities or any romance where the sports element is an integral part of the story. Use with: S* codes to indicate which sport is the key aspect of the romance story

Also class here: military, armed services, armed forces, security, sailors, aircrew, law enforcement, soldiers, sheriffs, cops, firefighters, police, pilots, cabin crew etc. Use for: romance stories where one or more of the main protagonists is in a job that means wearing a formal uniform
Use for: romance stories featuring doctors, nurses, surgeons, veterinarians, or any professional medical setting, such as a hospital or clinic, etc

Also class here: Rockstar romance, Rags to riches romance, Millionaire or Billionaire romance, Secret Billionaire romance, Celebrity romance, Royal romance. Use for: genres of romance fiction featuring persons in position of great wealth, power, status or similar, such as the jet set, super-rich, billionaires, royalty, aristocrats, rock stars, celebrities, high society, celebrity meets a non-celebrity and they fall in love, romance story featuring an ordinary person and a very rich, powerful, famous person, or romance fiction featuring at least one of the main characters who is royal or aristocratic or other inherited positions and titles, or featuring a royal kingdom or aristocratic domain, royal meets a non-royal and they fall in love, romance story featuring an ordinary person and an aristocratic or royal personage, etc. Use with: 5PDM* or other 5* INTEREST Qualifiers as appropriate

Also class here: ‘why choose’ romances, harem or reverse harem romances, polyamory romance. Use for: Romance or love stories featuring things like, open relationships, polyamorous relationships, polyandry, polyfidelity, consensual non-monogamy or non-exclusive relationships, or stories featuring multiple lovers, partners or romantic interests. Use with: VFVG2 for romances about polyamory, and with INTEREST 5* Qualifiers as appropriate

Also class here: vampire romance, were / shifter romance, supernatural romance, monster romance, alien romance, fantasy romance, paranormal romance. Use for: a romance story which blends elements from the fantasy genre or features mythical creatures or supernatural elements but remain primarily and recognisably a romance story, where the main plot revolves around a romance, with a fantasy or paranormal setting or with fantasy elements included. Use with: FM* or VXQ* codes as appropriate, for example for romance stories featuring a romance with vampires, werewolves or shapeshifters use with VXQM2, featuring demons with VXQM5, for angels, VXPS, ghosts, VXQG, witches VXWT, aliens VXQB, etc Ayrıca bakınız: FMR

Also class here: romance and love stories based on travelling to a past or future time via time loops, time machines, time slips, time portals, accidental time travel, alternate timestreams, time war, temporal paradoxes, experiencing time in reverse, communication from the future, being stuck in a time-loop, accidental time travel

Use for: genre romance stories where the themes are darker, usually featuring an anti-hero or non-heroic characters and/or distressing situations, often exploring themes such as the darker side of power dynamics in a relationship, questionable morals or ethics, they may feature trauma and violence, or they may deal with darker psychological themes of evil or horror in society. Use with: 5X if appropriate

Also class here: Rebel and outsider romance, Mafia romance, Mob romance, MC Romance, Motorcycle Club Romance, Rogues, Rebels, and Rakes romance, Bad boy romance, Bad girl romance, Alpha Male romance, Bully romance, Biker romance, MMA romance, Fighter romance, or romances featuring characters such as assassins, criminals, outlaws, bandits, or morally grey characters. Use for: romance genre stories where one of the main protagonist is often a very strong, possessive, confident, and dominant male or female character, or romances where the main character works for, or is involved with, crime or criminal organisations, or is seen as an anti-hero, a wrongdoer, an outsider, or to have a bad or dangerous character, or is morally ambiguous, but the “bad” character will usually have a redeeming side or a change during the story. Use with: FJ* for action and adventure stories, with FHR or FFL for romance stories featuring organised crime, and with INTEREST 5* Qualifiers as appropriate. Prefer: FRV for romance stories with darker themes Ayrıca bakınız: FRV
Romans marketine yönelik basılmış ama cinsel içerikli kurgular için kullanın; 5X kalifiyerleriyle de uygun olduğunda kullanılabilir Ayrıca bakınız: FP
Ev veya küçük ölçekli aile hayatı romanları için kullanın Ayrıca bakınız: FT

Bir ailenin ya da ailelerin hayatının genellikle nesiller boyu anlatıldığı romanlar için kullanın; İzlanda veya Norveç sagaları için kullanmayın. Burada sınıflandırın: Aile sagaları Ayrıca bakınız: FS
Mizahın ilk amaç ve özellik olduğu kurgular için kullanın; uygun olduğunda diğer F* kodlarıyla kullanılabilir
Satir amaçlı ve/ya varolan kurguların, yazarların veya türlerin parodilerini yapan mizahi kurgu için kullanın Ayrıca bakınız: WHP FYH

Geçmiş zamanda geçen çağdaş romanlar için kullanın, örn. 1900’ler öncesinde geçen, ancak türü-belirli olanlarda ‘tarihi’ başlıkları olabildiğince kullanın; uygun olduğunca diğer F* kodlarıyla kullanılabilir. COĞRAFİ ve DÖNEM kalifiyerlerini de romanın arkaplanını belirtmek için kullanın Ayrıca bakınız: FFH FJH FMH FRH
Belirli bir dini ya da ruhani mesaj verme kaygısı taşıyan kurgular için; uygun QR* veya VX* koduyla kullanılmalı
Kurgu eserin altta yatan anlatı temasını belirtmek için FX* kodlarını tür veya tipi belirten diğer F* kodlarının ardından kullanın
Burada sınıflandırın: Bildungsroman (oluşum romanı)

Code.CodeDescription: Narrative theme: books and the world of books
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: stories, novels and works of fiction where the main theme is about the world of books, including, booksellers, bookshops, libraries, literature, writers, the art of writing, books about reading, books about books, book clubs, publishers or any story that has a main theme taken from the world of books

Use for: fiction where a strong relationship or love is the central theme but which is not a genre romance novel. This can include friendships, found family, family relationships, sibling relationships, parent-child relationships, any form of affective relationship, relationships between couples, relationships that are negative or hostile, or complex emotional relationships, forbidden love, a love triangle, unrequited love, love of family, relationships amongst a group of friends or a peer group, examination of relationships with others, acquaintances, strangers etc, as long as it is one of the principal themes of the story. Use with: INTEREST 5* Qualifiers for detail of specific kinds of relationships as appropriate. DO NOT USE: with FR* codes
Belirli bir çevre sorununu merkezi tema olarak ele alan kurgu için kullanın

Use for: fiction or stories that feature animals or any living creature as a major or significant part of the plot or theme, or where human interactions or relationships with animals, including pets, is a main part of the plot, or one or more of the main characters or protagonists are animals. Use with: WN* codes if the story is about a specific type of animal, for example, WNGC for stories about cats, or WNGD for stories about dogs

Use for: works of fiction that take place during periods of war or armed conflict or civil strife, and where the experience or consequences of war, or battle or armed conflict is the major theme or topic of the story and is explored through the plot or the development of the main characters. Prefer: FJM* codes for action and adventure war fiction Ayrıca bakınız: FJM*

Use for: fiction where health, coping or living with illness – physical or mental – or the consequences of sickness is a central theme, or themes based on medical topics or suffering linked to physical or mental health, chronic illness or conditions, chronic pain, or themes around the healing, recovery or recuperation from illness
Kayıp ya da yas deneyiminin merkezi tema olduğu kurgu için kullanın
İç karakterizasyona ve karakterlerin güdü, duygu ve düşüncelerini özel olarak vurgulayan kurgu için kullanın. Psikolojik gerilimler için FHX kullanın Ayrıca bakınız: FHX

Use for: fiction where the identity, the sense of, or search for, identity of whatever kind – social, cultural, religious, gender etc, as an individual or part of a group – of the main character(s) is the main, or one of the main themes of the story, or narratives where the characters sense of belonging or search or need for belonging is the main or major theme of the plot. Use with: other subject codes and INTEREST 5* Qualifiers as appropriate
Siyasi alegoriler de dahil olmak üzere siyasi sorunların temel anlatı teması olduğu kurgu için kullanın. Siyasi gerilimler için FHX kullanın Ayrıca bakınız: FHP

Use for: fiction that has major themes relating to diasporas, dispersion, asylum, deracination, forced relocation, cultural transitions, forced journeys, living in exile, being exiled, emigration, expatriation, immigration, refugees, forced resettlement, etc Ayrıca bakınız: FXV

Gerçek bir yerde (mutlaka değilse de çoğunlukla kırsal ya da tarihi yerler) geçen ve bu yerin, eserin başka bir yerde kurgulanamayacağı ölçüde eserde ağırlık kazandığı kurgu için kullanın; örneğin, Fransız “kırsal roman” geleneğ. Uygun YER Niteleyicileri ekleyin
Belirli bir toplumsal sorun ya da konuyu merkezi tema olarak ele alan kurgu için kullanın

Code.CodeDescription: Narrative theme: diversity, equity, equality, inclusion
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: works of fiction where the main narrative theme or subject matter clearly illustrates topics relating to aspects of accessibility, social justice, equity or equality, diversity and inclusivity within the context of the story, or the story explores themes of DEI, or attempts to achieve DEI. Use with: other subject codes and INTEREST 5* Qualifiers to give greater detail as appropriate

Also class here: road trip stories, stories about voyages of exploration and discovery, stories about quests, epic journeys or about wanderers. Use for: fiction where a journey, expedition, voyage or some sort of travel or trip is the main or a major narrative theme of the story Ayrıca bakınız: FXQ
F* kodlarından sonra tür veya tip belirten FY* kodlarını kullanın
Also class here: Anthologies or collections of short works of fiction either by the same author or by multiple authors. Use with: DNT for anthologies of short stories by theme or by multiple authors
Use for: works of fiction that are neither seen as short stories nor as novels by their creators
Use for: fiction, literature, comic books or any fictional narratives that are written in a series of documents, letters, diaries, journals, emails, blogs, social media posts, etc

Also class here: Continuation novels. Use for: works of fiction where a new author continues an established series after the original authors death. These can be official with the permission of the literary estate or unofficial for works now out of copyright. These stories may be sequels to the original series or be stories that are prequels or precede the original storyline, but all the stories are written after the original authors death

Kasıtlı olarak başka (tipik olarak daha önceki) bir yazarın tarzında, genellikle bu asıl yazarın bir romanının devamı şeklinde veya yarattığı bir karakter kullanılarak (parodi değil saygı ifadesi olarak) yazılan kurgu için kullanın Ayrıca bakınız: FUP

Also class here: Past-Present narratives. Use for: fiction, literature, comic books or any fictional narratives that have storylines featuring two or more timelines (but where there is no time travelling or time slips), where a single cohesive narrative, is told using multiple time periods and perspectives

Use for: fiction, literature, comic books or any fictional narratives that are usually create an atmosphere of tension and suspense for the reader using psychological techniques and often feature themes things like a sense of fear and haunting, gloom or death, a dark past, a claustrophobic atmosphere, an oppressive, bleak, decayed or derelict setting, the threat of supernatural events, and the intrusion of the past upon the present and that often inspire fear through a romanticized view of the past, and often combining elements of both horror and romance etc. Use with: FR* for Gothic romance, FK* for Gothic horror, other F* codes for other types of Gothic fiction, with PLACE1* Qualifiers for gothic fiction associated with a particular area, such as 1KBB-US-S* codes - for Southern Gothic (USA) or 1KL* codes for gothic fiction set in Latin America

Var olan bir metni, genellikle klasik bir romanı, örneğin korku gibi başka bir karşıt tür ile tek bir anlatı şeklinde birleştiren kurgu için kullanın; birleştirilen ögeleri göstermek için diğer F* veya kurgu dışı kodlarıyla birlikte kullanın Ayrıca bakınız: FUP

Code.CodeDescription: Fiction based on or inspired by true events
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: fiction based on or inspired by a true event or happening but where this is told in narrative fictionalised form and is not just an account of the event itself. Use with: other F* codes to describe the genre or with Literature DB*, DC*, DD*, comic books XQ* codes. Prefer: DNX for narrative accounts of true stories, or FC for fiction based on peoples lives Ayrıca bakınız: DNX FC

Code.CodeDescription: Fiction: special features: yaoi / BL / danmei novels
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: boys’ love novels. Use for: East Asian style stories, often related to comics or anime, featuring male same-sex relationships, created principally, but not exclusively, for a female readership. Use with: other F* codes to indicate genre, for example FR* codes for Romance stories, 5LKE * codes if they are about that generation Ayrıca bakınız: XAMT

Use for: the kind of romance, science fiction or other types of genre fiction or comic books, usually published on a monthly basis, short, in clearly delineated lines and with a certain number published every month. Use with: other F* code indicating genre or type, for example, with FR*codes for Category or Series Romance. DO NOT USE: FYR as the main or primary subject or the only code

Also class here: Raito noberu, Japanese novellas, illustrated novellas. Use for: short fiction aimed at adults, usually driven primarily by dialogue and character and generally accompanied by illustrations in manga/anime or similar styles. Use with: other F* codes to indicate the genre. FYS may be used as a main subject as appropriate

Use for: fiction and literature translated from another language. Use with: F* or with Literature DB*, DC*, DD*, or comic book XQ* codes to ensure classification is meaningful beyond the translation of the work itself and with 5T* - Literature of Place Qualifiers as appropriate. DO NOT USE: PLACE 1* or LANGUAGE 2* Qualifiers to specify the original language (this is described in other metadata). You may still use a PLACE 1* Qualifier if it is relevant to the plot or setting of the book. DO NOT USE: FYT as the main or primary subject or the only code

Code.CodeDescription: Fiction: inspired by or adapted from other media
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: stories that were published as spin-offs or companions to pre-existing non-book media or merchandise, novelizations and novels inspired by a popular film franchise, an online game or a TV series. Use with: other F* codes indicating genre or type, or with Literature DB*, DC*, DD* codes if this work is presented as a poem or a play, or XQ* for comic book. DO NOT USE: for titles that were subsequently made into films, film tie-in versions (this is described in other metadata)

Code.CodeDescription: Fiction: special features: game-related / LitRPG stories
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: GameLit, RoLit, Game lit, literary role-playing game. Use for: fiction that is structured like a videogame or role playing game, or features the same kind of challenges as would be found in any type of game, or is about or set in a videogame, an online game, a role playing game, etc. Use with: other F* codes especially FL* or FM* as appropriate, or with Literature DB*, DC*, DD* codes if this work is presented as a poem or play or XQ* for comic book
Sınıflandırın: popüler kurgular için el kitapları, genel eleştiriden yoksun, eserin severlerine yönelik Ayrıca bakınız: DSR XR* DS*

belirli konusu olmayan eserler için kullanın

Belirli bir konuyu kapsayan sözlükler için kullanın, örneğin Hukuk sözlükleri

Use for: reference works that present a subject primarily through maps, charts, infographics, data visualisation, visual timelines or other mainly visual presentation of information. Use with: other subject codes for quantitative research methods or strategy within a particular discipline
Use with: other subject codes for qualitative research methods or strategy within a particular discipline

Use for: works about current debates, policies, ideas, controversies around the role of culture or cultural heritage in society, debates about clashes of cultural values or beliefs, debates about cultural imperialism, cultural diversity, the nature of culture, social and political policies linked to culture, debates about funding and political policies in culture
Use for: works that look at the expression, preservation, and change of human ideas over time. Use with: other J* or NH* or QD* codes as appropriate

Code.CodeDescription: Medya çalışmaları: İnternet, dijital medya ve toplum
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: all aspects of online, digital and social media and their role or impact in society, including things such as blogging, tweeting, influencers, spread of real and false information, changing habits and behaviour linked to digital media Ayrıca bakınız: ATN
Use for: works on both traditional and new forms of consuming small screen entertainment, including streaming and on demand services, impacts and influences on culture, links to popular culture, etc
Also class here: the Press, newspapers, news media, journalists and reporters, online and print journalism, communicating news and events Ayrıca bakınız: KNTP

Also class here: institutional racism, xenophobia, antisemitism. Use for: works about discrimination and prejudice based on skin colour, race or ethnic origin, or prejudices based on the perception that someone is foreign or from outside the community, and issues of inequality and discrimination, works that explore institutional or systemic racism, racial segregation, as well as measures to address racism, or to advance conversations about race, for works that look at other identities or perceptions of an identity, such as beliefs or religion, where the prejudice becomes or is treated as a form of racism. Use with: other J* codes for works about racism in particular domains and with 5P* INTEREST Qualifiers to indicate works about racism aimed at particular groups, for example, with 5PBD for works about racism aimed at those of African descent, with 5PGJ for works about racism aimed at Jewish people or on racial antisemitism, with 5PBA for works about racism against Indigenous groups, with 5PBR for racism against Romani or Travellers, etc

Use all Y* codes for: material aimed at, or purposefully written or created for a juvenile or adolescent audience (except for graphic novels, comic books, manga in X*). DO NOT USE: code ‘Y’ itself, but select specific categories from section Y*. Use all Y* codes with: only one INTEREST AGE 5A* Qualifier to indicate a guideline starting interest age (detailed age ranges should be included in other metadata) – or for YP* use EDUCATIONAL PURPOSE 4* qualifiers. All other qualifiers can be used as appropriate with Y* codes. DO NOT USE for: material intended primarily for adults that may also appeal to older teenagers. For ‘new adult’ content see note at 5LKE, for ‘Young Adult’ use the most appropriate 5A* Qualifier according to local usage of the term. NB: Y* codes should be used along with X* codes for graphic novels, comic books, manga. Y* codes may be used in combination with A*– W* codes but always prefer Y* codes and if mixing Y* codes with A*– W* codes, the Y* code must ALWAYS be designated as the Main Subject and sent with one 5A* qualifier. If sending A*– W* codes as Main Subject, then Y* codes should NOT be included except for JNU / JNUM with YP* or DSYC for reviews or critiques

Code.CodeDescription: Children’s / Teenage fiction: Magical realism / Magical fantasy
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: Magical girl. Use for: works that incorporates fantastic, magical, mythical or supernatural elements into an otherwise real-world or mundane setting, or works where the magic itself – whether a magical object or a character with magical powers – is the subject of the story, rather than simply a means to an end. Use with: YNXW for stories about witches, wizards or magicians or YNXB* codes for other magical creatures

Code.CodeDescription: Children’s / Teenage fiction: Mythic fantasy / Myths and Legends fiction
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: Myths or legends from any culture told or retold as fiction or in story form, mythological fiction, Arthurian fantasy, Classical fantasy (based on Greek and Roman myths), Shenmo (Gods and Demons), etc. Use for: fiction that is inspired by, or a retelling of, or that in some way draws from the characters, stories or themes of myth, legend, for example, a story based on a popular myth or character from a classic work in a modern setting or a story based on a minor character’s perspective, or that takes a ‘what if’ approach or create a mashup of different genres, for example, legendary character or hero meets dystopian future, or mythology crossed with contemporary adventure story. Use with: PLACE 1*, LANGUAGE 2*, INTEREST 5* Qualifiers to indicate if the story is taken from a particular tradition Ayrıca bakınız: YNRU YFJ

Also class here: Medieval, Dark Age, Arabian, Celtic, Gunpowder, Prehistoric, Wuxia fantasy. Use for: fantasy that incorporates fantastic elements, such as magic or supernatural beings, into recognisable historic settings, periods, cultures etc. Use with: PLACE 1* and/or TIME PERIOD 3* Qualifiers to indicate setting as appropriate
Burada sınıflandırın: Burada sınıflandırın: “Kara romans”, vampir romansı vb.; ayrıca uygunsa 5X de atayın
Use for: fantasy stories with darker and frightening themes, often incorporating elements of horror or that have a gloomy and threatening atmosphere or a sense of horror and dread

Code.CodeDescription: Children’s / Teenage fiction: Contemporary and urban fantasy
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: fantasy set in the present day or recognisably contemporary settings (according to the time period of its creator)
Burada sınıflandırın: Kurgu olarak anlatılan peri masalları, halk masalları, mitler ve efsaneler Ayrıca bakınız: YFHG

Code.CodeDescription: Children’s / Teenage fiction and stories: Folk and Fairy tales
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: Fairy tale retellings, fractured fairy tales. Use for: folk and fairy tales from any culture told in a story form, or retellings of these stories, stories inspired by fairy tales

Code.CodeDescription: Children’s / Teenage fiction and stories: Trickster tales
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: stories that feature a trickster character such as a spirit, a deity, a human or an animal

Code.CodeDescription: Children’s / Teenage fiction and stories: Creation, founding, origin stories
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: stories about the origins or beginnings of peoples, worlds, places, traditions, etc

Code.CodeDescription: Children’s / Teenage fiction and stories: Teaching stories
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: Cautionary tales, Wisdom tales. Use for: stories that were created for the transmission of wisdom, knowledge, cultural traditions, oral transmission of stories, or stories that warn or caution young people about specific dangers, to teach a lesson or a general moral issue

Also class here: Faith-inspired or inspirational stories. Use for: fiction that promotes a particular religious, spiritual or visionary message or viewpoint. Use with: 5PG* values from INTEREST 5* Qualifiers or YNR* codes, to indicate the religious tradition, as appropriate

Code.CodeDescription: Çocuk / Gençlik kurgu: Aşk ve ilişki hikayeleri
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: stories that deal with all kinds of relationships with others; for stories where interpersonal relationships are the main theme; or explore the relationship of the main characters, stories that explore relationships within groups, relationships between young people. Use with: YX* to give details of kinds of relationships as appropriate, for example, YXH for stories about relationships in peer groups or relationships with adults from a young persons perspective, 5PHG for stories about found or chosen family Ayrıca bakınız: YXHB
Use for: stories where the main or primary topic or theme of the narrative is the friendship between different child or teenage main characters

Code.CodeDescription: Children’s / Teenage fiction: Romance and love stories
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: contemporary romance, romantic comedy, romantic drama, stories of first or young love, teenage romances, teenage love-triangles, lost love, unrequited love, high school romance, etc. Use for: stories that are clearly of the romance genre and feature a romantic relationship as the core theme, that are specifically written for teenagers and deal with romance or love stories from a teenage point of view. Use with: YNX* codes as appropriate, with YFT and TIME PERIOD 3* qualifiers for Historical romance, with YFQ for comic romance, etc Ayrıca bakınız: YFHR

Code.CodeDescription: Çocuk / Gençlik kurgu: Aile ve yuva hikayeleri
Code.CodeNotes: YXF* aile sorunlarını işleyen kurgu sekansından kodlarla kullanın.

Code.CodeDescription: Çocuk / Gençlik kurgu: Doğa ve hayvan hikayeleri
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: stories featuring animals, or the natural world, or stories about human interaction or relationships with animals and the natural world, stories about the bond between a child and an animal or pet. Use with: YNN* codes to indicate what type of animal or nature story, for example YNNJ24 for Horse stories or YNN21 for stories about Dogs, YNNH* codes for stories about pets, YNNT for stories about plants or trees
Mümkünse türü belirten YF* kodlarından sonra kullanın
Use with: YNW* codes to indicate the sport in the story
Also class here: back to school, going to a new school, school life, stories principally taking place in and around school, etc. Use with: values from 5L* to indicate what school level as appropriate
Geçmişte geçen çağdaş romanlar için kullanın, örneğin 1960 öncesi için c seçin
Mümkünse türü belirten YF* kodlarından sonra kullanın
Mümkünse türü belirten YF* kodlarından sonra kullanın Ayrıca bakınız: YDP YBLB
Gerçek insanların yüksek düzeyde kurgusallaştırılmış biyografileri veya otobiyografileri için kullanın

Code.CodeDescription: Çocuk / Gençlik: Kurgu olarak anlatılan gerçek hikayeler
Code.CodeNotes: Burada sınıflandırın: Kurgudaki gibi güçlü bir anlatımsal biçimde yazılmış gerçek hikayeler (hayatta kalma hikayeleri, çatışma vb.)

Code.CodeDescription: Children’s / Teenage fiction / Literature / Comics / Graphic novels: Special features and related items
Code.CodeNotes: Use all YFZ* codes with: other YF* code indicating genre or type, YDP for poems, YNDS for plays, or YBCS for picture storybooks or XQ* codes for graphic novels, comic books or manga aimed at children or teenagers. NB: YFZ* codes should not usually be the primary or main subject code. DO NOT USE: YFZ itself - always use YFZ* codes

Code.CodeDescription: Children’s / Teenage fiction: Advent calendar stories
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: stories aimed at children or teenagers, usually in 24 or 25 chapters or stories, meant to be read, heard or seen as a countdown to Christmas through the Advent season. Use with: 5HPDA

Code.CodeDescription: Children’s / Teenage fiction: stories as diaries / journals / letters
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: Epistolary fiction. Use for: fiction, often with illustrations, written or drawn in a series of documents, letters, diaries, emails, blogs, social media posts, doodles, etc. Use with: other YF* or XQ* code indicating genre or type
Use for: stories that are reworkings, reimagining’s or retellings of stories, histories or tales. Use with: other YF* or XQ* code indicating genre or type

Code.CodeDescription: Children’s / Teenage fiction: category / serialised stories
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: genre fiction, or comic books usually published on a monthly basis, short, in clearly delineated lines and with a certain number published every month. Use with: other YF* or XQ* code indicating genre or type. YFZR codes should never be the main subject code

Also class here: Illustrated novellas. Use for: short fiction for children or teenagers, usually driven primarily by dialogue and character, and generally accompanied by illustrations in manga/anime or similar styles. Use with: other YF* codes to indicate the genre

Code.CodeDescription: Children’s / Teenage fiction: Stories in translation
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: fiction in translation from another language. Use with: YF*, YBCS, YDP, YNDS, or XQ* codes to ensure classification is meaningful beyond the translation of the work itself and with 5T* - Literature of Place Qualifiers as appropriate. DO NOT USE: PLACE 1* or LANGUAGE 2* Qualifiers to describe the detail of the original language, this would be described elsewhere and not using Thema. You may still use a PLACE Qualifier if it is relevant to the plot or setting of the book. DO NOT USE: YFZT as the main or primary subject or the only code

Code.CodeDescription: Children’s / Teenage fiction: Stories Inspired by or adapted from other media
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: stories that were published as spin-offs or companions to pre-existing non-book media or merchandise, for example story books based on a popular film franchise, toy, an online game or a TV series. DO NOT USE: for titles that were subsequently made into films etc. Use with: other YF*, YBCS, YDP, YNDS, or XQ* codes indicating genre or type. NB: YFZV codes should never be the main subject code

Code.CodeDescription: Children’s / Teenage fiction: Game-related / LitRPG stories
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: Literary Role Playing Game, GameLit, RoLit. Use for: fiction that is structured like a videogame, or features the same kind of challenges as would be found in a game, or is about or set in a videogame. Use with: other YF* or XQ* codes as appropriate Ayrıca bakınız: YFCA

Use for: companion works to popular children’s or teenage fiction series or titles, typically uncritical, such as an atlas or map of a mythical world or fictional universe, a compendium of characters or objects, a guide to the series, art inspired by or taken from the series etc. Use with: other Y* codes or on its own as appropriate, or with X* codes for companion works to graphic novels, comics, manga aimed at children or teenagers

YN* kodlarını başka kategorilere girmeyen tüm kurgu-dışı genel ilgi materyalleri olup , okulda kullanılmak için tasarlanmamışlar için kullanın. YN* kodlarını sadece kurgu-dışı eserler için veya uygunsa belirli konulardaki kurgu eserler için ilgili YF* kodundan sonra kullanın. YN* kodlarıyla birlikte mümkünse uygun 5A* Okuma Yaşı/Seviyesi niteleyicisi ve uygun diğer niteleyicileri kullanın.

Use with: 5PSG, 5PSL, 5PT, 5PU, 5PV, 5PW or other 5* INTEREST Qualifiers as appropriate or YF* codes for stories that are about these topics, any YN* or other YX* codes for general interest or non-fiction works, for example, YXA* for works about health or body, YNH for LGBTQIA+ history, YNB for biographies, YXQ* for works about violence or abuse based on LGBTQIA+ identity, etc

Use for: works that tell stories of, examine or give advice to young people about LGBTQIA+ person‘s process of, or journey to, recognition, personal acceptance and disclosure to others of their sexual orientation or gender identity. Use with: other subject codes and 5P* INTEREST Qualifiers as appropriate

Code.CodeNotes: Use for: books that deal with these topics and stories with a particularly diverse cast of characters, or which illustrate accessibility, social justice, equity, diversity, or inclusivity (DEI) within the context of the story without necessarily being the subject of the story. Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: discrimination, injustice, the judgements of others. Use with: YNH for historical topics

Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: physical, mental, emotional or sexual abuse, coercive control, domestic abuse, or works aimed at young people about criminal exploitation, debt bondage, exploitation of vulnerable children by criminal gangs

Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: online trolling and bullying, coercion, cyberbullying, cyberstalking, physical or verbal bullying or harassment, relational bullying, collective bullying or mobbing, bullies and accomplices, victims of bullying, effects of bullying and harassment, bystander effect, school bullying, victimisation

Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: Knife violence, gun violence, bombs, violent acts, acts of terrorism, kidnapping, violent threats, violent rampages. Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: fugitives, escapees. Use for: works that look at young people that run away and reasons around this, running away from home, or family or school or escaping things like repression, slavery, conflict, etc. Use with: YF* codes for stories about runaways, with YNB for biographies of runaways, or YNH for historical approaches Ayrıca bakınız: YXZM

Code.CodeDescription: Çocuk / Gençlik: Kişisel ve toplumsal sorunlar Okuldan kaçma ve okul sorunları
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: works that explore topics like starting school, attending school, going to a new school, school life, education topics, titles about teachers and educators, school librarians

Code.CodeNotes: Use for: works about issues at school, around repeated absence, non-attendance, avoiding school, etc

Code.CodeDescription: İlk gençlik kişisel ve toplumsal sorunlar: Kariyer ve ileri eğitim danışmanlığı, okuldan ayrılma

Code.CodeDescription: Children’s / Teenage personal and social topics: Growing up / coming of age
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: titles that deal with the changes from childhood or youth to adulthood, such as taking on adult responsibilities, career choices, character growth, gaining independence, self-reliance, moving away from home, going to university, first experience of love, etc. Use with: YF* for coming of age fiction, YXA* codes for works about changes to the body, or sex, YXHL for first love, etc

Also class here: social activism, general works on social justice. Use for: titles that deal directly with the topics or explain debates around social issues for young people. Use with: other YX* codes to give greater detail; YF* fiction codes for stories that are about these topics. NB: YXZ may be used with JBF* codes if there are no more precise Y* codes but if mixing YXZ with JBF* codes, a Y* code MUST be designated as the Main Subject and sent with a 5A* qualifier

Code.CodeDescription: Children’s / Teenage social topics: Activism / activists
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: titles about social activism, environmental activism, human rights, social or civil rights movements, causes and other forms of engagement as activists by young people, volunteering or volunteer engagement. Use with: other YN* or YX* codes to give greater detail and with YNB for biographies of activists

Code.CodeDescription: Children’s / Teenage social topics: Identity / belonging
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: titles that explore topics or themes around notions of identity and belonging, as individuals or as part of a particular group or communities, identity or belonging based on relationship to a place, based on a shared culture or heritage or other works that explore the notion of identity or belonging for children or teenagers

Code.CodeDescription: Children’s / Teenage social topics: Peace / reconciliation
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: works for young people about peace after conflict, maintaining peace, ideas for creating, keeping, spreading peace and peaceful actions, resolving conflict, themes and topics around reconciliation between different groups or persons

Code.CodeDescription: Children’s / Teenage social topics: Accidents, disasters or emergencies
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: either works about the impact or consequences, on both people and society, of both natural and human-made disasters and accidents; things such as diseases, plagues, epidemics, pandemics, famine, malnutrition, volcanic explosions, earthquakes, extreme-weather, floods, forced movement of peoples as a result of disasters; or works about accidents like fires, crashes, shipwrecks, maritime and air disasters or accidents, rail or road accidents, explosions, oil spills, getting trapped or lost, etc; or for titles that explain how to prepare for disasters, emergencies, etc for example, what to do during an earthquake, or major fire or tsunami

Code.CodeDescription: Children’s / Teenage social topics: Fame, celebrity, fandom
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: works for young people about fame, celebrity, being famous, the search for fame and the issues with being famous or a celebrity, being an idol, being glamorous or wealthy, or works about being a fan or fandom

Code.CodeDescription: Çocuk / Gençlik toplumsal sorunlar: Çevre ve doğa sorunları
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: looking after our planet, climate change, pollution, rubbish, plastics, recycling, climate emergency, climate strikes, environmental champions, looking after our future, protecting nature, conservation, water use and conservation, managing natural resources, sustainable solutions, reducing consumption and use of resources. Use for: works that look at these topics and also ones that have ideas for solutions, or what young people can do themselves

Code.CodeDescription: Children’s / Teenage: Social topics: Poverty / precarity
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: works that look at social issues topics in society around social instability, deprivation and hardship, homelessness, the unhoused, hunger, economically disadvantaged, food poverty, etc

Code.CodeDescription: Çocuk / Gençlik toplumsal sorunlar: Göç ve mülteciler

Code.CodeDescription: Çocuk / Gençlik toplumsal sorunlar: Dini sorunlar
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: titles that look at discussions, debates, topics, controversies, or other issues related to religion, belief, faith, religious identity, etc. Use with: YNR* or other Y* codes and 5PG* INTEREST qualifiers as appropriate

Code.CodeDescription: Çocuk / Gençlik toplumsal sorunlar: Savaş ve çatışma sorunları

Burada sınıflandırın: Genellikle dekoratif veya mizahi, çocuklar için hediyelik, küçük kitaplar

Code.CodeDescription: Children’s / Teenage: Miscellaneous non-book items: Games, puzzles or toys

Tekil kitaplarda ‘5’ kullanmayın, bölüm 5* kapsamındaki uygun niteleyicileri seçin

Use all 5A* age codes for: defining the Y* or X* codes – 5A* age numbers are used instead of named codes, such as juvenile, middle grade, young adult, as these have different meanings in different countries or languages. Select one 5A* code indicating a general guideline starting or base interest age of the content in any works aimed primarily at children or teenagers. All Y* codes (except YP* which use 4* codes) MUST be accompanied by one 5A* qualifier code to give guidance of interest age, for example: book content for an audience of 9 to 12 age group, should use 5AK, as the lower age; content of interest to teenagers should use 5AP or 5AQ; content for older teenagers and young adults should use 5AS, 5AT or 5AU as appropriate. 5AR, 5AX and 5AZ can be used with any relevant subject code. All 5A* codes can be used with X* subject codes if the Comic book is aimed at children or teenagers. DO NOT USE: 5A itself – always use 5A* codes. NB: Greater detail of age range, reading age, interest age etc would be communicated in other metadata

Also class here: High-low readers, Hi-Lo content aimed at children or teenagers. Use for: books that are specially written for or considered suitable for young people who do not want to read, have difficulty reading, or are struggling to read. Usually these books will have a higher interest age and a lower reading age. Content is usually aimed at a particular interest age but the language used is purposefully slightly simpler than most average content aimed at the same interest age in that language, so that it is easier to read or listen to than other titles. These are often titles in specific named collections and will often have notions of levels of difficulty associated with them by the publisher and / or may be accompanied by indications of complexity. Use with: one other 5A* Interest age qualifier. Prefer: 5AX for reluctant adult readers or 5AZ for accessible content and 4L codes for second language titles Ayrıca bakınız: 5AX 5AZ 4L*

Code.CodeDescription: Interest age: from c 17 years to c 29 years
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: works aimed specifically at older teens and young adults in their 20s, those who are newly adult, emerging adulthood. This age group may be referred to in some places as young adults or sometimes as new adults. The content is specifically created for and about this group but can also appeal to other groups as well. Prefer: 5LKE for titles about this age group. DO NOT USE: with Y* codes Ayrıca bakınız: 5LKE

Also class here: High-low readers, Hi-Lo content aimed at adults. Use for: books that are specifically aimed at adult literacy or helping adult readers with reading difficulties or books that are suitable for adult readers who are not confident in their reading abilities or suitable for the newly literate. Content is aimed at adult interests but the language used is purposefully slightly simpler than most average content aimed at adults so that it is easier to read or listen to than other titles

Code.CodeDescription: Content adapted or suitable for people with learning / communication difficulties or impairments
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: indicating works where the content is specifically adapted for, or purposefully written for, or aimed at people, regardless of age, with special or additional needs, who may have difficulty in accessing or reading the content of most titles. This could include content specifically adapted for people with, for example, dyslexia and other reading or learning disabilities, cognitive impairments or disorders, memory disorders, dementia or Alzheimer’s, visual or other sensory impairments, profound and multiple learning disabilities, etc. Use with: 5PM* Qualifiers as appropriate

Use all 5H* codes for: indicating that the content of a work is largely about or relates to the holiday, event or season, for example a book featuring a Christmas story would use 5HPD or a book about birthdays for children would use 5HKA, a romance story that is all about summer could use 5HRB. DO NOT USE: to create list of suggested titles for sale at a particular season (this is information that is conveyed elsewhere in the supply chain) if those titles do not have content relating to the 5H* code

Use for: content that is about public or civic holidays or celebrations in general or about a holiday or celebration that does not have a more precise code. Use with: 1* PLACE qualifiers when associated with a particular area

Also class here: Solar New Year festivals and ceremonies. Use for: titles about New Year traditions and celebrations from different calendars, cultures and regions. Use with: 5PG* codes for New Year celebrations associated with particular religious traditions or PLACE 1* qualifiers for works about traditions associated with particular geographical areas Ayrıca bakınız: 5HCC

Code.CodeDescription: Lunar New Year festivals and ceremonies
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: Matariki, Tsagaan Sar, Losar, Islamic or Hijri New Year, Kha b-Nisan, Naw-Rú

Also class here: Days, weeks or months of observance or commemoration. Use for: works about significant international, national or regional holidays, celebrations or days of remembrance, observance or commemoration, that mark a significant historical event or persons not covered by another 5H* code, including things like national celebrations that mark a revolution, a significant date for a religious figure associated with the country, a date associated with a significant personage from the past, etc. Use with: PLACE 1* Qualifiers to indicate works pertaining to a particular country

Also class here: Juneteenth National Independence Day, US National Freedom Day, International Day of Remembrance of the Victims of Slavery and the Transatlantic Slave Trade, International day for Remembrance of Slave trade and its Abolition, Season of Emancipation, Keti koti, August Monday. Code.CodeDescription: Relating to the stages of life
Code.CodeNotes: Use all 5L* codes for: indicating the content of the work has major themes, topics or storylines relating to or specifically about, or from the perspective of, the main stages of life, or the process of ageing, growing up, the cycle of life from birth to death, or fiction done from the point of view of a person or persons of that stage of life. A novel about teenage anxiety could use 5LF, a romance set amongst students at university could use 5LKE, or a book about Yoga for seniors could use 5LKS. DO NOT USE: to indicate a targeted audience for marketing purposes, the content should be primarily about this stage of life or age group or told from the point of view of that age group
Also class here: babies, infants and toddlers. Use for: material that has major or principal themes relating to, or from the perspective of, or primarily about infancy
Use for: material that has major or principal themes relating to, or from the perspective of, or primarily about childhood or being a child, or stories told from the point of view of a child

Use for: material that has major or principal themes relating to, or primarily about the years between childhood and adolescence, the passage from being a child to being a teenager, or stories told from the point of view of the preteen or preadolescence

Also class here: growing from a teenager to being an adult. Use for: material that has major or principal themes relating to, or from the perspective of, or primarily about adolescence or being a teenager, the teenage years, the issues, changes, developments that are common for teenagers. Use with: YF* or F* codes when the main themes of a novel are specifically related to the teenage years, being a teenager, specifically from a teenagers point of view, or issues connected with adolescence and use with non-fiction codes for studies, themes or content about teenagers

Use for: material that has major or principal themes relating to, or from the perspective of, or primarily about being an older teenager (roughly 15 to 19 years old), the later teenage years, the issues, changes, developments that are common for older teenagers, also referred to as young adults in some circumstances, post-adolescents. Use with: YF* or F* codes when the main themes of a novel are specifically related to the later teenage years, being an older teenager, specifically from an older teenager’s point of view, or issues connected with late or post adolescence and use with non-fiction codes for studies, themes or content about older teenagers
Use for: material that has major or principal themes relating to, or from the perspective of, or primarily about adulthood or being an adult, life as an adult, etc

Also class here: post-teens, new adult, young adulthood, twenty something, emerging adulthood, etc. Use for: material that is primarily about, or from the perspective of, or has major or principal themes relating to the stage of life spanning from the late teens through to the mid- or late twenties, often centred on topics around becoming an adult or coming of age, progressing from being a teenager to being an adult, those who are newly adult, learning to become an adult. Use with: FR* for ‘New Adult Romance’ or FRG for ‘College Romance’, FP for ‘New Adult Erotica’, FM* for ‘New Adult Fantasy’, etc. when the main themes of a novel are specifically related to this stage of life and use with non-fiction codes for studies, themes or content about this passage from teenager to adult
Use for: material that has major or principal themes relating to, or from the perspective of, or primarily about midlife or middle age

Code.CodeDescription: Relating to late adulthood / old age
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: seniors, elders, third agers, retirees, pensioners, older persons. Use for: material that has major or principal themes relating to, or from the perspective of, or primarily about old age or later life. Use with: F* or YF* codes when the main themes of a novel are specifically related to this phase of life, for example, FR* for romance in later life, or YFN for a story about an elderly relative, and use with non-fiction codes for studies, themes or content about this stage of life

Use all 5P* codes for: indicating the content of the work has major themes, topics or storylines relating to, or from the perspective of, or are specifically about the particular group of people. DO NOT USE: to indicate a target audience for marketing purposes, nor to identify the origin of the author, unless this relates to the content of the work

Belirli bir etnik grubun ilgi alanına giren ya da bu grupla ilişkili konuları olan ya da bu grup hakkındaki materyaller için 5PB* kodları kullanın; diğer konuların yanı sıra JBSL* kodlarıyla birlikte kullanın

Use for: material that has major or principal themes, topics or storylines relating to, or from the perspective of, or about, any groups of people or persons from any of the multiple, diverse and different groups or cultures of the various Indigenous communities, Peoples and Nations and where there is no more precise code. Use with: PLACE 1* Qualifiers as appropriate to indicate location or with LANGUAGE 2* Qualifiers when the language identifies the group, for example, a work about the Indigenous peoples of the Americas, use with 1K, for the Indigenous peoples of Mexico, use with 1KLCM, the Indigenous peoples of Peru, use with 1KLSR, for the Indigenous Peoples of the Arctic use with 1MTN, for Indigenous peoples of Siberia, use with 1FCS, for Indigenous peoples associated with the South -Western US States, use with 1KBB-US-WM, etc Ayrıca bakınız: 5PB-US-E 5PB-NZ-A 5PB-AU-A 5PBS

Also class here: Melanesians, Micronesians, Polynesians peoples, including, but not limited to, Kanaks, Papuans, Indigenous Hawaiians, Kānaka Maoli, Fijians, iTaukei, Ni-Vanuatu, Chamorro, Chuukese, Rapa Nui, Samoans, Tahitians. Use for: material that has major or principal themes, topics or storylines relating to, or from the perspectives of, or about, any of the diverse groups of people or persons, who are part of an Indigenous Pacific Island group or heritage

Use for: material that has major or principal themes, topics or storylines relating to, or from the perspectives of, or about, members of any Indigenous community who gained respect and stature through their lives allowing them to have a leadership role

Code.CodeDescription: Relating to peoples or groups of multiple heritage / culture
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: material where the major or principal themes, topics or storylines relate to, or from the perspectives of, or are about any of the diverse groups of people or persons of multiple heritage or cultures

Code.CodeDescription: Relating to migrant groups / diaspora communities or peoples / groups with shared heritage
Code.CodeNotes: Use all 5PBC* codes for: material where the major or principal themes, topics or storylines relating to, or from the perspectives of, or about, (historical and recent) diverse groups of people or persons who have migrated or were exiled or displaced from one part of the world to another; or are part of a diaspora community and who maintain a strong and distinct identity and cultural shared heritage associated with another geographical or cultural area within their present place of residence. Use all 5PBC* codes with: PLACE 1* Qualifiers as appropriate, to indicate the geographical area that is the subject of the work, usually where that group is now, for example, a title about Syrian migrant communities in Sweden, use with 1DNS, or a title about Guatemalan migrant workers in Mexico, use with 1KLCM or a study of German exiled writers of the mid-twentieth century, in the USA, use with 1KBB Ayrıca bakınız: 5PBD

Code.CodeDescription: Relating to people of the Middle Eastern diasporas / heritage
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: diaspora peoples of Western Asia, Anatolia, the Arabian Peninsula. Use for: material that has major or principal themes, topics or storylines relating to, or from the perspectives of, or about, (historical and recent) Middle Eastern diasporas, or any of the diverse groups or individuals of Middle Eastern heritage living in another geographical area or culture. Use with: PLACE 1* Qualifiers as appropriate, to indicate the scope of the geographical area covered by the group or individual or topic in the work, for example, a biography of an Armenian family in France, use with 1DDF*, or a novel about Turkish migrants in Germany, use with 1DFG*, or a history of Arab Americans in Detroit, use with 1KBB-US-MLGD. Prefer: 1FB* PLACE qualifiers, without 5PBCB, for works about peoples, groups or individuals who live in a particular Middle Eastern country or region, or works about peoples of the Middle East Ayrıca bakınız: 1FB*

Prefer: 1HB* PLACE qualifiers without 5PBCD for works about peoples, groups or individuals who live in a particular North African country or region, or works about peoples of North Africa Ayrıca bakınız: 5PBD 1HB*
